subject: Service resilience thresholds & remedy playbook — proposal
messages:
From: Elliot Burns <elliot.burns@auroracloud.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@auroracloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-27T11:12:00-05:00
Subject: Aligning on uptime target & monthly remedy structure

Hi Chloe / Laura,

Thanks for the conversation last week. Aurora is preparing the procurement packet for our 2028 deployment and we need to lock the service-levels and monthly remedy model before legal signs off. A few asks from our side: 

- Can Redwood commit to a 99.95% monthly availability target for the hosted inference endpoint (single-region for pilot)?
- If not, what incremental credit buckets would you propose for 99.9, 99.8 and below?
- How do scheduled maintenance windows and burst-driven performance degradations factor into credits (we need clear carve-outs)?

We tried to capture priority items in the attached procurement checklist. We'd also appreciate a short "remedy playbook" that explains escalation steps and expected timelines for credit processing — procurement prefers a predictable operational pathway rather than ad-hoc exceptions.

Can you send a proposed table and an escalation flow by EOD Monday? We're hoping to finalize commercial terms by mid-December.

Regards,
Elliot Burns
Head of Platform Partnerships
AuroraCloud

Attachment: aurora_procurement_checklist.pdf (procurement checklist, 2 pages)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Burns <elliot.burns@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-27T15:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on uptime target & monthly remedy structure

Elliot — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Appreciate the checklist; useful context.

High-level response and next steps (summary):

1) Availability target: We can offer a 99.95% monthly target for the pilot as a conditional commitment tied to (a) a dedicated capacity reservation and (b) a mutually-agreed maintenance cadence. The reservation ensures predictable capacity and routing.

2) Proposed remedy buckets (draft):
   - >=99.95%: no remedy
   - 99.90%–99.949%: 5% monthly service credit
   - 99.00%–99.899%: 15% monthly service credit
   - <99.00%: 30% monthly service credit (escalation to account + credits + root-cause remediation plan)

3) Maintenance and burst carve-outs:
   - Planned maintenance: 4-hour monthly window per region with at least 72-hour notice; maintenance inside that window is excluded from availability calculations.
   - Emergency maintenance and software rollbacks to mitigate active incidents will be documented and limited to qualifying events; these are eligible for post-facto review but not automatic carve-outs.
   - Burst-induced slowdowns: if telemetry shows transient queueing tied to customer traffic surges, we offer a partial credit model subject to a load-analysis threshold (we'll provide the threshold metric).

4) Remedy playbook & escalation path: attached a 2-page playbook that outlines triage, SLA measurement cadence, credit application timeline (30 days after confirmed incident), and a 3-step escalation path (CS -> Sales -> Exec sponsor call).

I've attached two artifacts: a compact resilience_playbook_v1.pdf and a proposed_sla_table.xlsx (breaks down the buckets and examples). Laura / Rishi — please weigh in on the monthly cap (we typically set a cap at 50% of monthly invoice for enterprise pilots, but we can adjust).

Next: happy to hop on a 30-min call — proposed times: Tue 11/29 10:00–11:00 ET or Tue 11/29 15:00–16:00 ET. Let me know which works.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: resilience_playbook_v1.pdf, proposed_sla_table.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Elliot Burns <elliot.burns@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28T09:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on uptime target & monthly remedy structure

Elliot / Chloe — quick note from legal/commercial perspective.

Chloe's buckets look good as a starting point. Two commercial asks from our side we should capture in the draft SLA: 

- Monthly cap: propose 50% of the monthly recurring invoice as a ceiling for aggregated credits (helps with runaway exposure).
- Root-cause remediation: for any incident triggering >15% credit, commit to a joint RCA within 14 business days and a remediation timeline with milestones.

Also, tighten the maintenance language: suggest we define a single "standard maintenance window" (e.g., first Saturday 02:00–06:00 UTC) for hosted pilot and then allow up to one ad-hoc emergency maintenance per quarter subject to notification. This reduces ambiguity for procurement teams.

I've attached a redline of the core SLA (redlined_sla_auroracloud.docx). If Aurora can accept the cap + RCA cadence, I think we can proceed to signature. Chloe — if you want me to make the DocuSign envelope, I'll draft it once we have final language.

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redlined_sla_auroracloud.docx

From: Elliot Burns <elliot.burns@auroracloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@auroracloud.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@auroracloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T10:50:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on uptime target & monthly remedy structure

Laura / Chloe — thanks, the draft looks solid and the playbook helps. A couple of clarifications from Aurora's side before we sign: 

1) We can accept a 50% monthly cap.
2) For latency: we need to add a complementary latency SLO (95th percentile p95 < 300ms for small requests) with a tied minor credit (2.5%) if the latency target is missed for two consecutive days. Can Redwood measure and report p95 latency at token-level and provide a weekly latency digest?
3) On maintenance: we can accept the single standard window but would ask for visibility into any capacity-planned upgrades (30-day notice) that might fall outside that window.

We're fine to move to signature once the latency clause is added and measurement/reporting expectations are defined. Can we do a short session to align on the telemetry fields? Our ops lead (Nina) will join.

Thanks,
Elliot Burns
Attachment: none

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Burns <elliot.burns@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Nina Park <nina.park@auroracloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T18:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on uptime target & monthly remedy structure

Elliot / Nina / Team — great, thanks for the clear feedback. Quick confirmation and action items: 

- Latency SLO: we can add a p95 < 300ms latency target for small requests (definition in the proposed_sla_table.xlsx: payloads < 1KB) with a 2.5% minor credit if missed for 2 consecutive UTC days. Redwood will publish a weekly latency digest (aggregated p50/p95/p99 per route) to the shared Drive.
- Measurement & telemetry: we'll share a telemetry schema (token-level latency, request id, model version, route) in the drive doc by EOD 11/30. That will be the canonical source for weekly digests and incident validation.
- Maintenance visibility: agree to 30-day advance notice for capacity-planned upgrades that could materially change availability; emergency maintenance remains limited and documented per playbook.
- Monthly cap: keep at 50% MRR. Credits applied as account credit within 30 days of incident confirmation.

I scheduled a 30-minute ops sync with Nina for Tue 12/02 11:00 ET (invite sent). Laura — please send the DocuSign envelope after we land the final latency clause; Rishi and I will review the redline tonight.

If that all looks good we'll finalize and route for signature. Thanks for the timely collaboration.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: resilience_playbook_v1.pdf, proposed_sla_table.xlsx
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-resilience-playbook, https://app.docusign.com/aurora/ACQ-2027-221
